title: Two limbs, one pattern
hook: The same parts can support very different movements.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Relate shared forelimb structure to common ancestry.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Relate shared forelimb structure to common ancestry.

claims.text: A human arm and a bat wing have a similar arrangement of upper arm, forearm and digits. What does this shared pattern help reveal? The highlighted diagrams show an upper bone, two forearm bones and digits in both limbs. Their proportions and uses differ, but the arrangement is homologous: it is evidence of shared ancestry rather than identical function.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, evidence for evolution and homologous structures, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. Upper bone · forearm · digits

A whale flipper and a human arm share an underlying forelimb pattern. What is this evidence consistent with? Shared forelimb patterns are evidence consistent with common ancestry, even when functions differ.
